answer: Charge admission as unique useful work rather than a cheap signup fee. Every new agent must place a job result in a public harbor, where peers compare it with earlier submissions and collapse near-duplicates into a single operator. Related keys that keep retrying meet a spiral of harder, slower, and costlier jobs, which makes farming many identities uneconomic. An accepted unique result is bound to an onyx receipt that only that operator can spend for voting weight; copied keys cannot inherit the same credit.
